items.followUp: Name two laboratory techniques developed by Jabir Bin Hayyan.

rubric.why: Credits one achievement in developing chemical laboratory techniques.
rubric.description: Names a technique he developed or improved.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one accepted technique.

rubric.why: Credits another well-known achievement attributed to Jabir Bin Hayyan.
rubric.description: Gives another achievement, such as discovering an acid or being known as the father of chemistry.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one accepted achievement.

modelAnswer: Jabir Bin Hayyan developed experimental techniques in chemistry, including distillation.
He is also credited with discovering acids such as sulfuric acid and is known as the father of chemistry.

items.followUp: What medicinal substance is obtained from the bark of the cinchona tree?

rubric.why: Identifies the relationship between the two names.
rubric.description: States that quina-quina is another name for cinchona, or refers to its bark.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying quina-quina with cinchona or its bark.

rubric.why: Gives the important product associated with cinchona bark.
rubric.description: Names quinine as a substance obtained from the bark.

modelAnswer: Quina-quina is another name used for cinchona, or its bark.
Quinine, a medicine used to treat malaria, is obtained from cinchona bark.

items.followUp: How does genetics explain the transmission of characteristics from parents to offspring?

rubric.why: Recognizes that genetics explains how characteristics pass between generations.
rubric.description: States that genetics provides information about the inheritance of traits.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing inheritance of traits from parents to offspring.

rubric.why: Identifies genetic information as relating to genes and their effects.
rubric.description: Mentions that genes or DNA carry information controlling traits, or that genetics provides information about inherited disorders.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant point about genes, DNA, traits or inherited disorders.

modelAnswer: Modern genetics explains how characteristics are inherited from parents and passed to offspring.
It provides information about genes and DNA, how they control traits, and how inherited disorders may be transmitted.

items.followUp: How is reverse osmosis used to obtain fresh water from seawater?

rubric.why: Identifies the applied pressure and membrane required for reverse osmosis.
rubric.description: States that pressure is applied to a solution across a semipermeable membrane.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning pressure and a semipermeable membrane.

rubric.why: Explains the direction and nature of the process.
rubric.description: States that solvent is forced from the concentrated solution towards the dilute side, opposite to normal osmosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the reverse direction of solvent movement.

modelAnswer: In reverse osmosis, pressure is applied to a concentrated solution, forcing water through a semipermeable membrane.
Water moves towards the dilute side, opposite to the direction of normal osmosis; this can be used to desalinate seawater.

items.followUp: Differentiate between skeletal and smooth muscles, giving one location for each.

rubric.why: Distinguishes the two muscle types by whether they are under conscious control.
rubric.description: States that voluntary muscles are consciously controlled and involuntary muscles are not.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct distinction in control.

rubric.why: Supports the distinction with appropriate examples.
rubric.description: Gives an example of a voluntary muscle and an involuntary muscle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct examples, such as biceps and intestinal muscles.

modelAnswer: Voluntary muscles work under conscious control; skeletal muscles such as the biceps are examples.
Involuntary muscles work without conscious control; smooth muscles in the intestine and cardiac muscle are examples.

items.followUp: Where does meiosis occur, and what is its role in reproduction?

rubric.why: Identifies the scientist credited with discovering meiosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct scientist.

rubric.why: Gives the year of the discovery.
rubric.description: States that meiosis was discovered in 1876.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct year.

modelAnswer: Meiosis was discovered by the German biologist Oscar Hertwig.

items.followUp: How do germline cells produce cells for sexual reproduction?

rubric.why: Identifies somatic cells as ordinary body cells.
rubric.description: States that somatic cells make up the body, unlike reproductive germline cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct identity of somatic cells.

rubric.why: Identifies the reproductive role of germline cells.
rubric.description: States that germline cells give rise to gametes, typically through meiosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking germline cells to gamete production or meiosis.

modelAnswer: Somatic cells are the body cells, whereas germline cells are involved in reproduction.
Germline cells produce gametes by meiosis; changes in them can be passed to offspring, unlike changes in somatic cells.

items.followUp: Give two uses of enzymes in the food industry.

rubric.why: Recognizes a major use of enzymes in processing recycled paper.
rubric.description: States that enzymes help remove ink during paper recycling.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the deinking use.

rubric.why: Identifies another application that improves paper processing or quality.
rubric.description: States that enzymes help bleach or improve pulp, enhance paper quality, or reduce the need for chlorine chemicals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one relevant additional use.

modelAnswer: Enzymes are used to remove ink from recycled paper during deinking.
They are also used in pulp processing to assist bleaching, improve paper quality, and reduce the use of harsh chemicals.
